findings.claim: Row r4 lacked evidence for six of its checks.
The apt test missed chromium on the install line itself.

verdict.text: Both round 1 findings are fixed.
The r4 evidence is now recorded from the operator's check of the live 0.23.4-1 deployment.
The apt test reads every apt-get install argument.
The re-signed r3 is met by the new paragraph in hermes.md.
The change can be committed.
f2: I replayed the new test logic against five versions of the Dockerfile.
It catches chromium on its own line, after `--no-install-recommends` on the install line, and beside jq.
Removing jq is also caught.
The real Dockerfile passes.
f1: the operator reported each r4 check on 2026-11-27.
A voice note was transcribed.
A memory search returned memories through openviking_tools and the sidecar, which can only work if the plugin loaded.
A Medium link was read through browser_exec, partly, because of the paywall.
The bot listed the cron jobs, and the dashboard sign-in completed.

The `/cron` substitute holds: upstream v0.23.4 gateway/session_commands.py line 52 has `_OWNER_COMMANDS = frozenset({'cron'})`, which makes `/cron` an owner command, so the cron tool listing is the right check.
Round 1 already confirmed the healthy deployment in Nomad.

r3 (re-signed, judgment): the hermes.md history paragraph says the operator applied without a state.db copy, that v0.23.3 moved the schema from 31 to 33, and that there is no restore point to 0.22.2-3.
No page claims a copy exists.

I am relying on the coordinator's report that the stamp is green.
I re-ran `uv run --directory cli pytest` (828 passed) and `kmctl check` (all checks passed).
The code under review only changed in the test file and hermes.md.
